cards.title: Simulation Types: Typical vs. Mean vs. Uncertainty
cards.claim: Simulations based on fixed-effect estimates illustrate the profile for a typical individual, which generally differs from the population mean prediction. Mean latent-population predictions average over the specified between-subject parameter and relevant covariate distributions, by simulation or suitable integration; measurement residual error is conditional on the requested observed-data estimand. Parameter uncertainty simulations represent uncertainty in estimated parameters and resulting exposures or covariate effects, while BSV simulations describe the distribution of individual predictions.
conditions: Applicable when defining simulation objectives for human PK/PD.
Typical simulations use only fixed-effect parameters.
BSV simulations require random effects; residual error models are required only when predicting observed concentrations.
Uncertainty simulations require estimates of parameter precision (e.g., bootstrap, standard errors).
required_inputs: Between-subject variability (BSV) estimates (variance/covariance of random effects).
Parameter uncertainty estimates (e.g., covariance matrix of fixed effects).
limitations: Typical profiles do not represent the population mean.
Ignoring BSV in mean predictions leads to underestimation of exposure range.
Parameter uncertainty is distinct from biological variability; conflating them misrepresents risk.
cards.downstream_use: Select the appropriate simulation type based on the specific question (e.g., typical profile for mechanism, BSV for dose range, uncertainty for confidence intervals).
cards.retrieval_keywords: Typical exposure versus between-person variability versus parameter uncertainty

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
